isaias-chamado-is-01-visao-do-trono.context: Isaiah sees the Lord in the year King Uzziah died. An earthly king dies, but the eternal King is on the throne, surrounded by worship, and calls a man of unclean lips.
isaias-chamado-is-01-visao-do-trono.focusQuestion: Seeing the Lord as he is, what do you need to confess and surrender to him?
isaias-chamado-is-01-visao-do-trono.keywordGloss: Repeated three times by the seraphim, it shows the Lord set apart from everything and worthy of worship.
facts: Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a high and exalted throne.
Each seraph had six wings.
The seraphim proclaimed the holiness of the Lord of Hosts.
Isaiah acknowledged he was a man of unclean lips.
With the coal on his lips, Isaiah's sin was forgiven.

isaias-chamado-is-02-aqui-estou-eu-envia.context: After being forgiven, Isaiah hears the Lord ask who will go for him. His answer is ready, but the mission he receives is hard and long, until only a stump remains.
isaias-chamado-is-02-aqui-estou-eu-envia.focusQuestion: Do you offer yourself to the Lord even without knowing whether the task will be easy or hard?
isaias-chamado-is-02-aqui-estou-eu-envia.keywordGloss: The answer of one who, forgiven, makes himself available to the Lord before knowing the details.
facts: Isaiah heard the Lord ask whom he would send.
Isaiah answered by offering himself to be sent.
The people would hear without understanding and see without knowing.
The desolation would last until the cities were deserted.
From the felled remnant a stump would remain, the holy seed.

isaias-esperanca--01-o-emanuel.context: In a time of threat, the Lord himself announces a sign, a son called Immanuel. Isaiah also speaks of a Servant who would carry the pains and iniquities of others.
isaias-esperanca--01-o-emanuel.focusQuestion: Where do you need to remember today that God has not abandoned you?
isaias-esperanca--01-o-emanuel.keywordGloss: Name of the son announced as a sign that God is with his people.
facts: The Lord himself would give the people a sign.
The virgin would conceive and bear a son.
The son would be named Immanuel.
The Servant was wounded for transgressions that were not his.
The Lord laid on the Servant the iniquity of us all.

isaias-esperanca--02-o-servo-sofredor.context: Isaiah describes a despised Servant, with no beauty to attract us, who suffers in silence and carries what belonged to others. The end is not defeat, but fruit and intercession.
isaias-esperanca--02-o-servo-sofredor.focusQuestion: What changes in you when you know that someone carried what was yours?
isaias-esperanca--02-o-servo-sofredor.keywordGloss: The one who, in Isaiah 53, suffers in the place of many and is called Righteous by the Lord.
facts: The Servant was despised and the most rejected among men.
Oppressed and humiliated, the Servant did not open his mouth.
The Servant never did injustice, nor was there deceit in his mouth.
The Servant will justify many, bearing their iniquities.
He poured out his soul to death and interceded for the transgressors.

isaias-esperanca--03-desafio-isaias.context: This challenge reviews Isaiah: the sign of Immanuel and the suffering Servant. God announces his presence and shows a Servant who carries the pains and sin of others, and intercedes.
isaias-esperanca--03-desafio-isaias.focusQuestion: In reviewing Isaiah, what truth about God do you want to keep and obey today?
isaias-esperanca--03-desafio-isaias.keywordGloss: Name of the sign of God with his people, linked in Isaiah to the Servant who suffers for many.
facts: The son announced as a sign would be named Immanuel.
The Servant was despised and the most rejected among men.
The Lord laid on the Servant the iniquity of us all.
Oppressed and humiliated, the Servant did not open his mouth.
The Servant never did injustice, nor was there deceit in his mouth.
He interceded for the transgressors after giving himself to death.
